minutes.headline: Sewer Commission leaned toward an 8% rate increase for FY23 to cover a projected deficit; numbers to be rerun at 6% and 8%.
minutes.summary: The commission went line by line through the draft FY23 sewer enterprise budget, which shows an operating deficit and a larger deficit once betterment revenue against debt service is included. Members discussed the proposed 3% rate increase, agreed it was too low, and most favored about 8%, with an annual-increase policy suggested. No formal vote on rates; the manager was asked to run 6% and 8% scenarios for the next meeting, and only adjournment was voted.

budget_items.what_was_said: Draft user charges revenue is based on current customers and expected new connections, including the irrigation meter annual fee.
The draft assumes a 3% rate increase after a 10% increase in 2021, which the commission questioned.
If all stays the same the draft shows a deficit including debt service, capital reserve transfer, OPEB transfer and capital spending.
Leominster usage is the biggest cost increase, near last year's budget.
Connection charges budgeted far below prior-year receipts since new connections are unpredictable.
Budget includes fees charged only to non-compliant accounts; charging all would be more.

Includes year three of pump station contract and generator maintenance; rise questioned versus FY21.

Reduced from last year's amount; members discussed lowering further given expected ARPA money but kept it open.
Leominster debt service and usage estimates are flow dependent and bumped modestly.
Town accountant's estimate includes health insurance assumed to rise and family coverage for new hire.
Expenses against projected revenue show a deficit if nothing changes.

what_happened.line: Commission members agreed a sewer rate increase is needed for FY23, with most favoring about 8% and some 5-7%; no vote was taken.
The manager was asked to run the numbers at 6% and 8%, with capital spending and engineering reviewed, for the Feb 22 meeting.
The draft FY23 budget assumes a 3% rate increase and shows an operating deficit once debt service and transfers are included; members questioned the 3%.
The budget is to be finalized by March 8, ahead of the Finance Committee presentation.
The only vote was adjournment; the next meetings were set for Feb 22 and March 8 at 6 pm, remote.

why_it_matters: Sewer charges are paid by connected households and businesses, so a rate increase would raise those users' bills, and the rate the commission lands on depends on how much of the deficit it chooses to close through rates.
The commission was discussing a deficit that includes debt service and betterment revenue, so the size of the rate change turns on those lines as well as day-to-day operating costs.
